title: Esacriats
reviewNotes: Reconstructed the seven-piece position after ...Kxb1. Checked the full bishop/king staircase to Bc2 mate, a waiting-move stalemate, and a losing pawn capture. The preceding rook sacrifice remains source context.
transcript: White sacrifices a rook for a knight, but after the king takes, it doesn't seem like there's a way for white to prevent these pawns from being pushed and promoted. Once the king gets back out, the pawn is going to be pushed and black will win. But that was the whole point of sacrificing the rook because white can now play [music] bishop to D3 with a check. And because of the other bishop, the king is forced to go to A2. And now, [music] with a little maneuver, we can block the king, bishop to C4 with another check. The only move is to come back to B1. And now, bishop to B3 takes away both of these squares, and the dark square bishop still takes away the C1 square. But black is not out of moves quite yet. Black can still play pawn to [music] A2. And now, actually, there is a big problem for white. You see, if you play a random waiting move like bishop to E3, this would end the game instantly because the black king has no squares that it can go to, and none of these pieces can move. So, this would be a draw by stalemate. So, white needs to make sure that rather than stalemate, he's going to find a checkmate. But to avoid the stalemate, black needs to have at least one legal move available. But the moment we move this bishop away, black is just going to come out and threaten to get a new queen. We cannot allow that, so we would need to push the king back inside. So, is this it? Is this position simply a draw? Well, not exactly because of white has a brilliant idea to convert this into a win. And that idea starts with the majestic king to G5. But of course, we can take away the view of the [music] bishop with our own king, and in the process, we can get the king closer. And after every new check, the black king will have to go back to B1. So, we continue with this pattern, and we get the king closer and closer by blocking the view of the bishop one move at a time. And eventually, once the king reaches D3, we can now support a check by the light square bishop and deliver bishop to C2. Checkmate. Follow me for more incredible chess.
